chunks: A number from our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn Umar al-Sayqal, from Abu Shu'ayb al-Mahamili, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'A time will surely come upon the people in which the debauched will be treated with delicacy/respect, and the immoral will be brought near [to power], and the fair-minded will be weakened.' He said, and it was said to him, 'When will that be, O Amir al-Mu'minin?' He said: 'When the trust (al-amanah) is taken as a gain, and Zakat as a loss, and worship as a protracted engagement, and maintaining ties of kinship as a favor.' He said, and it was said, 'When will that be, O Amir al-Mu'minin?' He said: 'When women become dominant, and bondmaids are empowered, and young boys assume command.'
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of societal decline and inversion of values according to Imam Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam Ali (as) outlines the signs of the 'Inversion of Values' (Qalb al-Ni'am), where administrative competence is replaced by status-seeking, and religious obligations like Zakat are viewed as financial losses. This era of decay is specifically triggered by the rise of the unqualified to power—symbolized by women, slaves, and children—reflecting the Shia scholarly understanding of the breakdown of justice (Adl) and the usurpation of authority by those lacking wisdom.

en.hubeali: H 14473 – A number from our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Musa Bin Umar Al-Sayqal, from Abu Shuayb Al-Mahaamily, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman who said:

Abu Abdullahasws having said that ‘Amir-ul-Momineenasws said: ‘An era will come upon the people in which, the debaucher (pervert) would be considered respectable, and nearness would be sought for the immoral, and fair play would be weak’. He (the narrator) said, ‘I said to himasws, ‘When would that be, O Amir-ul-Momineenasws?’ Heasws said: ‘When an entrustment would be regarded as a gain and the Zakat as a loss, and the worship as a protracted (engagement), and the maintenance of good relations as a favour’. He (the narrator) said, ‘I said to himasws, ‘When would that be, O Amir-ul-Momineenasws?’ So heasws said: ‘When the women become dominant, and the bondmaids would be empowered, and the young boys would assume command’.
